theorem_title: ℒ itself has all the Theorem D properties, and Diaz's conjecture holds exactly when no non-zero element of ℒ has algebraic modulus
formal_statement:
open Complex ComplexConjugate

namespace DiazModulus

theorem span_logAlg_theorem_D_properties :
    (DiazModulusConjecture ↔
      ∀ u ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg, u ≠ 0 → ¬ IsAlgebraic ℚ ((‖u‖ : ℝ) : ℂ)) ∧
    /- conjugation -/
    (∀ z ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg, conj z ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg) ∧
    /- (D2) Baker -/
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → ℂ), (∀ i, l i ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg) → LinearIndependent ℚ l →
      ∀ (b₀ : ℂ) (b : Fin n → ℂ), IsAlgebraic ℚ b₀ → (∀ i, IsAlgebraic ℚ (b i)) →
        (b₀ ≠ 0 ∨ ∃ i, b i ≠ 0) → b₀ + ∑ i, b i * l i ≠ 0) ∧
    /- (D2) Hermite-Lindemann -/
    (∀ z ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg, IsAlgebraic ℚ z → z = 0) ∧
    /- (D2) Gel'fond-Schneider -/
    (∀ l₀ β : ℂ, l₀ ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg → β * l₀ ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg → l₀ ≠ 0 → IsAlgebraic ℚ β →
      ∃ q : ℚ, β = (q : ℂ)) ∧
    /- (D3) Roy, relative to ℒ: strong six exponentials for ℒ̃ gives it for span Q̄ (insert 1 L) -/
    ((∀ (x : Fin 2 → ℂ) (y : Fin 3 → ℂ),
        LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) x → LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) y →
        ¬ (∀ i j, x i * y j ∈ LogAlgTilde)) →
      ∀ (x : Fin 2 → ℂ) (y : Fin 3 → ℂ),
        LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) x → LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) y →
        ¬ (∀ i j, x i * y j ∈ Submodule.span Qbar (insert 1 ((Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg : Submodule ℚ ℂ) : Set ℂ)))) ∧
    /- (D3) six exponentials -/
    (∀ (x : Fin 2 → ℂ) (y : Fin 3 → ℂ), LinearIndependent ℚ x → LinearIndependent ℚ y →
      ¬ (∀ i j, x i * y j ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg)) ∧
    /- (D4) four exponentials in transcendence degree one -/
    (∀ l₁₁ l₁₂ l₂₁ l₂₂ : ℂ, l₁₁ ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg → l₁₂ ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg → l₂₁ ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg → l₂₂ ∈ Submodule.span ℚ LogAlg →
      l₁₁ ≠ 0 → l₁₂ ≠ 0 → l₂₁ ≠ 0 → l₂₂ ≠ 0 → l₁₁ * l₂₂ = l₁₂ * l₂₁ →
      Algebra.trdeg ℚ ↥(Algebra.adjoin ℚ ({l₁₁, l₁₂, l₂₁, l₂₂} : Set ℂ)) ≤ 1 →
      (∃ a b : ℚ, ¬(a = 0 ∧ b = 0) ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₁ = 0 ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₂ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₂ = 0) ∨
      (∃ a b : ℚ, ¬(a = 0 ∧ b = 0) ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₁₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₁₂ = 0 ∧ (a : ℂ) * l₂₁ + (b : ℂ) * l₂₂ = 0)) := by
  sorry

end DiazModulus
source: Not found in the sources read as a bundle. The clauses are Baker's theorem (A. Baker, Linear forms in the logarithms of algebraic numbers I, Mathematika 13 (1966), 204–216); Hermite–Lindemann (Ch. Hermite 1873; F. Lindemann 1882); Gel'fond–Schneider (A. O. Gel'fond 1934; Th. Schneider 1934); the six exponentials theorem (S. Lang, Introduction to Transcendental Numbers, Addison-Wesley, 1966, chapter II; K. Ramachandra, Contributions to the theory of transcendental numbers I, II, Acta Arith. 14 (1968)); the four exponentials theorem in transcendence degree one (M. Waldschmidt, Solution du huitième problème de Schneider, J. Number Theory 5 (1973), 191–202; W. D. Brownawell, The algebraic independence of certain numbers related by the exponential function, J. Number Theory 6 (1974), 22–31); the Roy clause is an implication from Roy's strong six exponentials theorem (D. Roy, Matrices whose coefficients are linear forms in logarithms, J. Number Theory 41 (1992), 22–47, Cor. 2). Uses DiazModulus.mem_logAlg_adjoin_circle_point_iff, Schanuel.baker_linear_forms_in_logarithms, DiazModulus.hermite_lindemann_holds, Schanuel.gelfond_schneider, DiazModulus.six_exponentials, DiazModulus.four_exponentials_trdeg_one and DiazModulus.logAlg_conj_stable. R19 of the Diaz modulus mission. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 October 2026 (C. Perassi).
